def test_do_algebra():
    # Basic addition
    assert do_algebra(['+'], [3, 4]) == 7
    assert do_algebra(['+'], [0, 0]) == 0
    assert do_algebra(['+'], [-1, 5]) == 4

    # Basic subtraction
    assert do_algebra(['-'], [10, 4]) == 6
    assert do_algebra(['-'], [4, 10]) == -6
    assert do_algebra(['-'], [5, -3]) == 8  # 5 - (-3)

    # Basic multiplication
    assert do_algebra(['*'], [3, 4]) == 12
    assert do_algebra(['*'], [0, 100]) == 0
    assert do_algebra(['*'], [-2, 6]) == -12

    # Integer (floor) division
    assert do_algebra(['//'], [9, 2]) == 4
    assert do_algebra(['//'], [100, 10]) == 10
    assert do_algebra(['//'], [7, 3]) == 2

    # Operator precedence: multiplication before addition
    assert do_algebra(['+', '*'], [2, 3, 4]) == 14  # 2 + 3*4
    assert do_algebra(['*', '+'], [2, 3, 4]) == 14  # 2*3 + 4

    # Subtraction before division
    assert do_algebra(['-', '//'], [20, 8, 3]) == 17  # 20 - 8//3

    # Multiple operators, mixed precedence
    assert do_algebra(['+', '*', '-'], [2, 3, 4, 5]) == 5  # 2 + 3*4 - 5
    assert do_algebra(['//', '*'], [12, 3, 4]) == 16       # 12//3 * 4

    # Longer chains
    assert do_algebra(['+', '+', '-'], [1, 2, 3, 4]) == 2  # 1+2+3-4
    assert do_algebra(['*', '*', '+'], [2, 3, 4, 5]) == 29 # 2*3*4+5

    # Negative operands
    assert do_algebra(['+'], [-5, -5]) == -10
    assert do_algebra(['*', '-'], [-2, -3, -4]) == -10  # (-2*-3) - -4 = 6+4

    # Single operand (no operators)
    assert do_algebra([], [42]) == 42

    print("All tests passed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_do_algebra()
